story.title: Saudi Arabia Faces Houthi Attacks on Energy Facilities
story.summary: Saudi Arabia is experiencing increased pressure from Houthi attacks targeting airports and energy facilities. The Iran-aligned Houthi militia has threatened to strike the Saudi energy giant Aramco following an evacuation notice issued by Saudi authorities for an oil facility in Yemen's capital. This situation raises questions about the potential success of a Saudi-led international military offensive against the Houthis.

timeline_highlights.title: Trump Issues Threats Against Iranian Infrastructure Amid Strait of Hormuz Tensions
timeline_highlights.summary: US President Donald Trump has threatened to target Iranian bridges and power plants in retaliation for any attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. He stated that for each ship fired upon by Iranian forces, the US would respond by destroying a corresponding piece of Iranian infrastructure. This escalation comes amid ongoing tensions in the region and rising oil prices.
key_facts: Trump threatened to destroy Iranian infrastructure for each ship attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
The threat follows continued Iranian attacks on shipping in the region.
Oil prices have surged amid the escalating tensions.

timeline_highlights.title: Saudi Arabia Suspends Flights Following Houthi Missile Attacks on Riyadh Airport

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is the 2026 armed conflict that began with U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran on February 28, followed by Iranian retaliatory attacks and a widening regional security crisis. It has included fighting affecting Iran and neighboring Gulf states, as well as repeated threats to commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz; diplomatic contacts and temporary arrangements have not resolved the underlying conflict.

facts.label: Start and status
facts.value: The current phase of the conflict began on February 28, 2026. The International Maritime Organization described the Strait of Hormuz crisis as unresolved on August 28, six months after the conflict began.

facts.label: Main parties and geography
facts.value: The conflict centers on military action by the United States and Israel against Iran and Iranian retaliatory activity across the region. Its regional effects have included attacks or alleged attacks involving Gulf states and risks to shipping in the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, and Strait of Hormuz.

facts.label: U.S. military operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command calls its campaign against Iran Operation Epic Fury. The U.S. government has said the operation was directed at Iranian military and security targets and was intended, among other stated purposes, to protect U.S. forces and maritime commerce through the Strait of Hormuz.

facts.label: Strait of Hormuz significance
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz is a major international shipping passage whose traffic-separation scheme was proposed by Iran and Oman and adopted by the International Maritime Organization in 1968. The IMO says attacks, disruptions, and safety risks in the strait have left seafarers and vessels exposed during the conflict.

facts.label: International response
facts.value: The United Nations Security Council addressed the escalation on February 28, 2026, and the UN Secretary-General called for de-escalation, dialogue, and adherence to international law and international humanitarian law. The IMO has separately urged states and maritime actors to protect civilian seafarers and restore safe navigation.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on late-July 2026 escalation, U.S. war-powers debate, Houthi-linked developments, and ceasefire-related diplomacy; it does not attempt to cover the full military, humanitarian, legal, or diplomatic record of the conflict.
